audience.text: Python developers building 3D content processing pipelines, especially in 3D printing, CAD, and visualization workflows.

capabilities.text: Supports importing OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, COLLADA, and 3MF, and exporting to OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, and 3MF via Scene.open() and Scene.save().
capabilities.title: Load and save multiple 3D formats

capabilities.text: Construct and traverse a scene graph using Scene, Node, and Entity objects with independent transforms per node.
capabilities.title: Build and edit scene graphs

capabilities.text: Build meshes from control points and polygons, convert primitives to meshes, and triangulate arbitrary polygon data.
capabilities.title: Create and manipulate mesh geometry

capabilities.text: Attach LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial to nodes and configure diffuse, specular, albedo, metallic, and roughness properties.
capabilities.title: Assign materials with PBR support

capabilities.text: Build keyframe animations using AnimationClip, AnimationNode, and KeyframeSequence, and store skeletal bind-pose data.
capabilities.title: Support keyframe animation

capabilities.text: The library has no required third-party package dependencies and runs on Python 3.7+ without native runtime requirements.
capabilities.title: No external dependencies

limitations.text: FBX import is experimental and FBX export is not implemented; FbxExporter.save() raises NotImplementedError.
COLLADA export is not reachable through Scene.save() due to exporter lookup order issues.
Scene.render() and the entire aspose.threed.render module raise NotImplementedError.
Texture construction raises NotImplementedError; image-backed textures cannot be created.
Mesh boolean operations (union, difference, intersect) raise NotImplementedError.
NURBS curve evaluation and surface-to-mesh conversion raise NotImplementedError.

problems_solved.text: Enables programmatic import and export of common 3D formats (OBJ, STL, glTF/GLB, COLLADA, 3MF) using a pure-Python API.
Provides a scene graph model with nodes, transforms, entities, and materials for constructing and editing 3D content.
Supports building meshes from control points and converting parametric primitives to editable mesh geometry.
Enables material assignment and PBR workflow support for glTF and other formats.

product_summary.text: Aspose.3D FOSS for Python is a pure-Python, MIT-licensed library for loading, constructing, and exporting 3D scenes without native dependencies.

uncertainties: Whether the library supports importing FBX files in practice beyond tokenizer-level tests.
Whether COLLADA export works when bypassing the standard Scene.save() path.
Whether the public types for unsupported formats (PDF, PLY, USD, etc.) have any functional implementation beyond raising RuntimeError.
Whether the Scene.open() auto-detection works reliably for formats without explicit FileFormat hints when filenames are ambiguous.

workflows.name: Import and inspect 3D scenes
workflows.text: Open a 3D file using Scene.open() and traverse its node hierarchy to inspect geometry and structure.

workflows.name: Export scenes to common formats
workflows.text: Save a constructed scene to OBJ, STL, glTF, or 3MF using Scene.save() with appropriate SaveOptions.

workflows.name: Build meshes programmatically
workflows.text: Create meshes from control points and polygons, then attach them to scene nodes with optional materials.

workflows.name: Construct and convert primitives
workflows.text: Instantiate parameterized primitives like Box, Sphere, Cylinder, and convert them to editable meshes.

workflows.name: Assign materials to nodes
workflows.text: Attach LambertMaterial, PhongMaterial, or PbrMaterial to nodes and configure their color and factor properties.
